# SpThreshold: Replication Threshold for Bayesian Multilevel Models of Areal Data

## Part I: Replication threshold via m_star()

[1] Load the package and set the seed:

```{r}
library(SpThreshold)
set.seed(2026)
```

[2] Generate a random connected adjacency matrix:

```{r}
n <- 100
W <- create_random_W(n_locs = n)
```

[3] Set the residual variance, nonspatial random-intercept variance, and spatial correlation. The spatial variance scale is obtained through variance calibration:

```{r}
sigma2 <- 0.50
tau_ns_2 <- 0.50
rho <- 0.70

cal <- variance_calibration(
  W = W,
  rho = rho,
  tau_ns_2 = tau_ns_2
)

data.frame(
  tau_ns_2 = cal$tau_ns_2,
  tau_sp_2 = cal$tau_sp_2
)
```

[4] Compute the approximate threshold under three covariate structures. Covariates are centered and standardized to population variance one.

* C1: Independent covariate values, with most variation within areas:

```{r}
m_obs <- 20
N <- n * m_obs
loc <- rep(1:n, each = m_obs)

X_c1 <- rnorm(N)
X_c1 <- (X_c1 - mean(X_c1)) /
  sqrt(mean((X_c1 - mean(X_c1))^2))

res_c1 <- m_star(
  W = W,
  sigma2 = sigma2,
  rho = rho,
  tau_ns_2 = tau_ns_2,
  X = X_c1,
  loc = loc,
  method = "approx"
)

res_c1$m_star
```

* C2: Covariate variation both within and between areas:

```{r}
loc_means <- rnorm(n)
X_c2 <- rnorm(N, mean = loc_means[loc], sd = 1)
X_c2 <- (X_c2 - mean(X_c2)) /
  sqrt(mean((X_c2 - mean(X_c2))^2))

res_c2 <- m_star(
  W = W,
  sigma2 = sigma2,
  rho = rho,
  tau_ns_2 = tau_ns_2,
  X = X_c2,
  loc = loc,
  method = "approx"
)

res_c2$m_star
```

* C3: Covariate variation only between areas:

```{r}
X_c3 <- loc_means[loc]
X_c3 <- (X_c3 - mean(X_c3)) /
  sqrt(mean((X_c3 - mean(X_c3))^2))

res_c3 <- m_star(
  W = W,
  sigma2 = sigma2,
  rho = rho,
  tau_ns_2 = tau_ns_2,
  X = X_c3,
  loc = loc,
  method = "approx"
)

res_c3$m_star
```

[5] Compare the approximate and exact thresholds under C2. The exact threshold identifies the replication level at which the full conditional variance difference remains within tolerance for every larger sample size:

```{r}
res_c2_exact <- m_star(
  W = W,
  sigma2 = sigma2,
  rho = rho,
  tau_ns_2 = tau_ns_2,
  X = X_c2,
  loc = loc,
  method = "exact"
)

data.frame(
  m_approx = res_c2_exact$m_approx,
  m_exact = res_c2_exact$m_exact
)
```

[6] Vary $\rho$ under C2, holding $\tau_{\mathrm{ns}}^2$ and $\sigma^2$ fixed:

```{r}
rho_seq <- c(0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95)

m_star_rho <- sapply(rho_seq, function(r) {
  m_star(
    W = W,
    sigma2 = sigma2,
    rho = r,
    tau_ns_2 = tau_ns_2,
    X = X_c2,
    loc = loc
  )$m_star
})

data.frame(
  rho = rho_seq,
  m_approx = m_star_rho
)
```

[7] Vary $\kappa=\tau_{\mathrm{ns}}^2/\sigma^2$ under C2:

```{r}
k_seq <- c(0.05 / 0.95, 0.50 / 0.50, 0.95 / 0.05)

m_star_k <- sapply(k_seq, function(k) {
  m_star(
    W = W,
    sigma2 = 1 / (1 + k),
    rho = rho,
    tau_ns_2 = k / (1 + k),
    X = X_c2,
    loc = loc
  )$m_star
})

data.frame(
  kappa = k_seq,
  m_approx = m_star_k
)
```

[8] Vary the tolerance $\gamma$ under C2:

```{r}
gamma_seq <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)

m_star_gamma <- sapply(gamma_seq, function(g) {
  m_star(
    W = W,
    sigma2 = sigma2,
    rho = rho,
    tau_ns_2 = tau_ns_2,
    X = X_c2,
    loc = loc,
    gamma = g
  )$m_star
})

data.frame(
  gamma = gamma_seq,
  m_approx = m_star_gamma
)
```

[9] An adjacency matrix can also be constructed from a shapefile. This example uses the North Carolina shapefile included in `sf` and requires the `sf` and `spdep` packages:

```{r}
library(sf)

shp_path <- system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf")
polygons <- st_read(shp_path, quiet = TRUE)
W_nc <- create_W_from_shapefile(polygons)

dim(W_nc)
```

## Part II: Model fitting via spfit()

The function `spfit()` fits spatial or nonspatial multilevel models using MCMC.

[1] Generate a Gaussian dataset with covariate variation within and between areas:

```{r}
set.seed(2026)

n_locs <- 50
m_per <- 10
N <- n_locs * m_per

W_small <- create_random_W(n_locs)
loc_small <- rep(1:n_locs, each = m_per)

beta_true <- c(0.50, 1.50)
sigma2_true <- 0.50
tau_sp_2_true <- 0.50
rho_true <- 0.50

D <- diag(rowSums(W_small))
Q_true <- rho_true * (D - W_small) +
  (1 - rho_true) * diag(n_locs)

theta_true <- as.numeric(
  t(chol(tau_sp_2_true * solve(Q_true))) %*% rnorm(n_locs)
)
theta_true <- theta_true - mean(theta_true)

loc_means_x <- rnorm(n_locs)
x_small <- rnorm(N, mean = loc_means_x[loc_small], sd = 1)
x_small <- (x_small - mean(x_small)) /
  sqrt(mean((x_small - mean(x_small))^2))

X_small <- cbind(1, x_small)
colnames(X_small) <- c("(Intercept)", "x")

y_small <- as.numeric(
  X_small %*% beta_true + theta_true[loc_small]
) + rnorm(N, sd = sqrt(sigma2_true))
```

[2] Fit the spatial model:

```{r}
fit_sp <- spfit(
  y = y_small,
  X = X_small,
  loc = loc_small,
  W = W_small,
  model_indicator = 1,
  mcmc_samples = 15000,
  burnin = 5000
)
```

[3] Summarize the posterior after burn-in:

```{r}
summary_sp <- posterior_summary(fit_sp)

summary_sp[, c(
  "parameter", "mean", "median", "variance", "lower", "upper"
)]
```

[4] Fit the nonspatial model to the same data:

```{r}
fit_ns <- spfit(
  y = y_small,
  X = X_small,
  loc = loc_small,
  W = W_small,
  model_indicator = 0,
  mcmc_samples = 15000,
  burnin = 5000
)

summary_ns <- posterior_summary(fit_ns)

summary_ns[, c(
  "parameter", "mean", "median", "variance", "lower", "upper"
)]
```

[5] Compare the marginal posterior variances of the covariate coefficient using the retained MCMC draws:

```{r}
draws_sp <- posterior_draws(fit_sp)
draws_ns <- posterior_draws(fit_ns)

var_sp <- var(draws_sp$x)
var_ns <- var(draws_ns$x)
rel_diff <- abs(var_sp - var_ns) / var_ns

data.frame(
  variance_spatial = var_sp,
  variance_nonspatial = var_ns,
  relative_difference = rel_diff,
  gamma = 0.05,
  within_tolerance = rel_diff <= 0.05
)
```

[6] Compute the approximate and exact thresholds using the generating spatial covariance parameters and the calibrated nonspatial variance. These thresholds describe the full conditional variance comparison at fixed covariance parameters:

```{r}
res <- m_star(
  W = W_small,
  sigma2 = sigma2_true,
  rho = rho_true,
  tau_sp_2 = tau_sp_2_true,
  X = x_small,
  loc = loc_small,
  method = "exact"
)

data.frame(
  m_actual = m_per,
  m_approx = res$m_approx,
  m_exact = res$m_exact
)
```

[7] The data-frame and matrix interfaces give the same coefficient draws when supplied with the same data and random seed:

```{r}
df_small <- data.frame(
  y = y_small,
  x = x_small,
  area = loc_small
)

set.seed(7)
fit_df <- spfit(
  data = df_small,
  formula = y ~ x,
  area = "area",
  W = W_small,
  model_indicator = 1,
  mcmc_samples = 15000,
  burnin = 5000
)

set.seed(7)
fit_vec <- spfit(
  y = y_small,
  X = X_small,
  loc = loc_small,
  W = W_small,
  model_indicator = 1,
  mcmc_samples = 15000,
  burnin = 5000
)

identical(fit_df$beta, fit_vec$beta)
```

## Part III: Two-stage procedure

Apply the two-stage procedure to the same dataset, treating the covariance parameters as unknown.

[1] Estimate the covariance parameters:

```{r}
two_stage <- two_stage_estimate(
  y = y_small,
  X = X_small,
  loc = loc_small,
  W = W_small
)

two_stage$estimates
```

[2] Examine the full conditional variance comparison at the observed design:

```{r}
two_stage$conditional_variances
```
